production.note: US model years, from Cars.com (a database), whose MC20 history lists the '2025', '2024', '2023' and '2022 Maserati MC20'. First: The Drive's review of the '2022 Maserati MC20' (thedrive-mc20-2021) and KBB's 'all-new 2022 Maserati MC20' (kbb-mc20-2022). Last: Motor1: "For 2026, Maserati has tweaked the MC20 and given it a new name, MCPura" (motor1-mcpura); the MCPura is not part of this record, nor is the MC20 Cielo, sold under its own name.

body.note: Two-seat fixed-roof coupe with butterfly doors. The open MC20 Cielo is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

displacementL.note: Maserati: "Displacement (cc) 3000 cc". Evo's specification panel gives "V6, 2992cc, twin-turbo" (evo-mc20); both round to 3.0.

drivetrain.note: 'RWD'; Maserati release: 'Rear-wheel drive with rear limited slip self-locking mechanical differential'

powerHp.note: Quote (Maserati USA): "Max power: 621HP [2]", footnote "[2] Max Power: metric HP at 7.500 rpm". Maserati's launch release (stellantis-mc20-release): "Max. power output 630 CV @ 7500 rpm"; 630 x 0.98632 = 621 hp, the figure Maserati USA prints. powerStandard is DIN PS because the rating is the metric 630 CV, as for the McLaren records.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (weight-order step 4). Quote (Evo specification panel, Adam Towler and Yousuf Ashraf, 25 September 2025): "Weight | 1475kg (dry)". 1,475 kg x 2.20462 = 3,252 lb. Coupe, 8-speed DCT (the only transmission). Evo does not say whether this is with options. Steps 1 to 3 are not met: Maserati publishes only upper limits, "an extremely lightweight car under 1,500 kg (kerb weight)" and "homologated weight (kg) <1500kg" (stellantis-mc20-release), and Maserati USA "Total Car Weight: < 3620lb" (maserati-us-mc20). The Drive (Ronan Glon; Basem Wasef) and MoparInsiders (Robert S. Miller) print "3,306 pounds", which is Maserati's 1,500 kg upper limit converted, not a curb weight (thedrive-mc20-2021, thedrive-mc20-2022, moparinsiders-mc20). A car ready to drive is heavier than the dry figure.

discrepancies.reason: Maserati states only upper limits ('under 1,500 kg (kerb weight)', '< 3620lb'). The Drive and MoparInsiders print 3,306 lb, which is the 1,500 kg limit converted and so not a curb weight. Evo's panel gives a dry weight of 1,475 kg.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Evo's dry 1,475 kg (step 4), since no curb weight, exact or for an optioned car, exists; the upper limits are noted only.
